newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits softer before jobless claims.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits softer before jobless claims.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were slightly lower in thin trade with most traders sidelined before today's issue of the U.S. weekly jobless claims data, dealers said on Thursday.
Weekly jobless claims for the week ended May 17, are forecast to be around 324,000 compared with 319,000 reported in the previous week.
"Rates were a little bit softer this morning on some position adjustments, amid uncertainty over the near-term direction of the market," a local dealer said.

"Some people are waiting for fresh clues to market direction from today's weekly jobless claims figures, but unless the numbers are way off market expectations, I don't think there will be much impact," he said.
In short dates, Thursday/Friday slipped 1/8 percentage point to 5-9/16 5-7/16 percent.
Weekend and week-fixed eased 1/16 point each to a common 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent, respectively.

Among term rates, one-month eased 1/16 point to 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent, three-months eased 1/16 point 5-13/16 5-11/16, nine-months eased 1/16 point to 6-1/16 5-15/16 and twelve-months eased 1/16 point to 6-3/16 6-1/16 percent.
